newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Key Australian senator faces fraud charges.
newsitem.headline: Key Australian senator faces fraud charges.

text.p: Australian authorities said on Tuesday they have issued summonses against key independent Senator Mal Colston over allegations of fraud.

"The director of public prosecutions has given notice that summonses have been issued against Senator Mal Colston in relation to allegations of fraud against the Commonwealth (government)," Attorney-General Daryl Williams said in a statement.
The charges relate to travel claims and the use of frequent flyer points, Williams said.
Williams would not comment further, saying the issue would go before the courts next month.
A conviction could change the balance of power in parliament's upper house, the Senate, where the government is in a minority, because it would make Colston ineligible to continue in parliament.
Colston's vote has been vital to government legislation passing the upper house Senate, where the ruling Liberal-National coalition does not have a majority.
Colston was elected to the key post of deputy Senate president -- with government support -- after he defected from the Labor opposition last year to sit as an independent.
But he was forced out of that post when the government joined Labor and other minority parties in turning against him over allegations he had abused parliamentary benefits.
Although Colston is now an independent, he would have to be replaced by a Labor Party member, because he was elected as a Labor senator.
Williams said former government senator Noel Crichton-Browne would also be charged over separate fraud allegations.
"Mr Crichton-Browne is being summonsed on charges...in relation to allegations of defrauding the Commonwealth on matters associated with spouse travel entitlements," Williams said.
